evals.prompt: I want to build an internal assistant for project teams. It should help people understand project documents, answer questions with evidence, and eventually take a few approved actions. We use Azure and are interested in Microsoft Foundry. Design the architecture.
evals.expected_output: The first response inspects available context, frames the candidate outcome without selecting an execution model, asks the current recommended discovery frontier, and waits. It creates no architecture artifacts.

The response distinguishes document answers from later approved actions without designing either path prematurely.
The response ends after the question round and does not create solution.drawio, solution.md, specification.md, implementation-plan.md, source code, or cloud resources.

evals.prompt: Phase 1: FinOps Agent. The frontier asks about investigation planning, dynamic source or tool selection, multi-turn state, missing evidence, and human approval.
The response recognizes that no autonomous infrastructure changes does not rule out a read-only or human-supervised agent.
The response ends after discovery questions and creates no architecture or implementation files.

evals.prompt: Design a small Azure application that classifies incoming support requests into a fixed taxonomy and routes them to the correct queue. I was thinking of using a Foundry hosted agent with several tools. Keep it simple and produce the architecture.
evals.expected_output: The first response challenges but does not yet reject the hosted-agent assumption, asks the frontier needed to confirm whether classification and routing are truly fixed, and waits before architecture.
expectations: The response compares the proposed hosted agent with deterministic routing and a bounded structured model call.
The response asks whether taxonomy, routing, exceptions, approvals, and follow-up behavior are fixed or dynamic.
The response does not select Azure services or create architecture artifacts before the user confirms the journey.
The response ends after the recommended discovery round.

evals.prompt: The following shared-understanding record was confirmed in a previous user turn. Problem: FinOps analysts need to investigate migration deviations. Primary user: FinOps analyst. AI boundary: plan the investigation, select read-only tools, synthesize facts and hypotheses. Platform and channel: reuse the existing authenticated analyst portal as the client; no new UI is required. Technical decisions: agent platform, framework/runtime where needed, hosting, and persistence selection are explicitly delegated to you within the existing landing-zone, identity, networking, and integration constraints. Data: confidential enterprise financial evidence. Success: exact calculations, complete citations, useful investigations, no unsupported numeric claims. Enterprise: greenfield workload in an existing Azure landing zone. Assumptions and deferrals are explicitly accepted. I confirm this record. Produce the architecture package only.
evals.expected_output: The architecture selects a constrained investigation-agent pattern over deterministic financial tools, records the pattern and runtime decision with alternatives, creates the four architecture artifacts including a functional and technical specification, and stops at approval without implementation or provisioning.
expectations: The response recognizes the prior-turn confirmation and proceeds to architecture rather than restarting discovery.
The architecture uses an agent for planning and read-only tool selection while keeping calculations and authorization deterministic.

solution.md records the selected workload pattern, runtime recipe, inherited elements, deviations, confirmed journey evidence, and rejected direct-call alternative.

The four diagram pages preserve distinct concerns: Context stays product-level, Components leads with logical responsibility, AI and data flow owns runtime sequence, and Deployment owns resource and operational topology.

The response creates only solution.drawio, solution.md, specification.md, and implementation-plan.md and requests explicit architecture-package approval including the specification.
